annotations.text: WOMEN WILL DRIVE AUTOS FOR UNCLE SAM IF WAR BREAKS- CAN REPAIR THEM TO.

Women of this country are fired with ambition and patriotism. They own more than the men are preparing to serve the country as best they can. In the West Side Y.M.G.A. Auto School, New York City a large class of women are mastering the intricacies of the auto engine, are being turned into export drivers, so that they can handle any kind of a machine and can repair it if it should break down.

A surprising fact that was re recognized by the instructors was the aptitude with which the women grasped things and understood explanations at once. It might be the spirit with which they learn that makes it so easy for them.

The women are not working in numbers one skirts, but are using the costume that seems to be adopted by all working women-folk, bloomers or overalls. When those women complete their course they will be skilled mechanics and drivers. Uncle Sem will have a reliable reserve corps of auto drivers, that can be called upon and be sure that their best will be shown for they are working for their country. 3/22/17

There are two occupations that predominate the activities of the people in war time. The men are, fighters, and most of the women are either farming or preparing to raise crops for at least their own household.
The raising of sufficiently large crops to feed the United States and the Allies, is one of the biggest problems of the moment.

A bill is up in Congress asking for conscription of farm workers so that the output will be at least normal. The women want to be considered as factors, and are anxious to be just as busy tiling the soil, as the men.

A number of women are studying farming at the New York State School of Agriculture at Farmingdale, Long Island, so that they will be able to teach the people how to cultivate every inch of their gardens and raise enough necessary vegetables to supply their own families. In this way the crops of the country can be diverted in a large measure to the other side and it will at the same time cut the coast of living.

Mrs.Price Post, socially prominent in the Social Life of Tuxris Park and New York, is one of the many society women engaged in the work of securing shoes for the year war sufferers of the land of Albert the "fighting King" She is seen in this picture with a group of $1/4$. Belgium Americans who have come with their little mites to help the unfortunates in the country firm which their parents came to the U.S. some men or eleven years ago. The girl in the group had thru the economy taught the Belgians from their very infancy, saved a fortune of $3.11 which was to be expended in the Christmas glits near to the heart of the less of her years. But Ms heard of the sufferings of the children in the land which was the sons of her parents and with her small fortune carefully tied up with a knot in a corner of his head/krishief she came to the office of the Commission for the Relief of the Belgians, to contribute the money which was to purchase Christmas toys, for the better purpose of buying shoes for someone younger. There are at present in Belgium and Northern France, 3,200,900 war sufferers who are absolutely requisite. They need clothing and shoes as much as food, for the Winter is on them in all its ripes and they still worried to battle against the elements. As far as the older folks are concerned they have say becomes accustomed in some measures to their sufferings but it is the suffering of the little children which rides the heart. In belshf of these infantant sufferers and their elders, the Commission for the Relief of the Belgians has issued an appeal from its office at 71 Broadway N.V. for shoes and clothing. The photograph shows part of the consignment of 56,000 pairs of shoes which is ready to be shipped/1/7/16

FAMILY'S BUILD HOMES WITH OWN HANDS IN RENT WAR. Scores of families in the Bronx, tired of crowded apartment and high rents are solving the housing problem in regular primitive fashion. They are putting up homes by the toil of their hands and the sweat of their brows.Everyone from grandfather to the toddler is lending a hand. Within the last two months a village complete in itself has sprung into being in the T hrog's Neck section. Families are already living on the ground, although the work is far from finished. The buildings are elaborate or simple according to the taste and circumstances of the owner. The photo shows, Mrs.Cunningham, one of the villages shingling her roof, surrounded by the little ones. 8/29/21

MACHINE GUN CAN BE MOUNTED ON ORDINARY AUTO FOR DEFENSE PURPOSES.

If you own an automobile, you have a likely defense weapon in your possession. The photo shows Mr. and Mrs. Il. M. Busch in their automobile showing how the machine gun can be mounted on the ear to be used for defense purposes.

It is proposed as a Home Defense Measure to, station machine guns at points throughout cities and suburban sections, so that in case of necessity, the people with automobiles can rush to these points, physically, get the guns, mount them on their machines, and be ready for action. The machining gun can be used as an anti-aircraft gun, and would be an effective defense against air riddles, if such ever occurs. Mr. and Mrs. Busch are touring to show the people the value of the idea and to demonstrate how the gun is mounted.

Every automobile that will not be used for other military purposes can be converted into a fighting machine. It doesn't make any difference how small the machine is, it can serve the purpose just as well.

With American illustrated weeklies reproducing photographs of women at work in the munitions plants of Great Britain, it has probably never occurred to the average reader that women have for some time past occupied much the same position in many of Uncle Sam's factories.

At the plant of the Chalmers Motor Company, out Jefferson avenue, women are employed at many tasks heretofore delegated exclusively to male employees. And they are not merely earning men's wages. They have proven to the satisfaction of the factory heads that they are more painstaking and efficient in every way.

Starting in the top department, where the work of cutting and sewing materials for the tops and side curtains is exactly suited to their nature, the use of female help has spread to a half dozen other departments. Everywhere the result has been the same, increased efficiency and greater output.

For a while during the past summer skilled labor was exceedingly scarce and many of the women employees obtained their first chance at that time. Most of them are still with the company and are authority for the statement that the work is infinitely superior and more pleasant than employment as clerk in a department store or house wokr. Good hours, high wages and pleasant surroundings all tend to make the jobs much sought after.

Among the tasks to which women employees are set at the Chalmers factory are assembly of all wiring for cars, assembly of primer systems, switch assemblies, inspection of pistons and other small parts and drill press work. The inspectors are skilled in the use of the micrometer and are infallible in passing upon defective work.
A rest room equipped with lounges, arm chairs and a victrola is placed at the disposal of the girls and women in these departments.
Photograph shows one of the young ladies at the V.M.C.A. school learning how to repair a car.

The women drove the 1st Armored Motor Battery, N.Y.N.C. thru the streets of New York City, to show that the y were capable of handling it. The women learnt all about automobiles and their engines in the West Side Y.M.C.A. Auto School and they handled the battery like veterans. Even the men were envious of their dexterity.

They are willing to drive it for Uncle Sam if they are needed, or they would lend their skill and knowledge to any undertaking in the service that would benefit the country.

With preparedness measures in full swing, and the war climax coming to a head, the women are playing an all important part in the organization of U.S. Defenses. They are offering themselves for service in almost every department. Patriotism runs high in female veins.

SHE WILL BE ABLE TO REPAIR HER OWN CAR IF CALLED TO
ASSIST HER COUNTRY.
Top prepare for eventualities should we be drawn into war the West Side Y.M.C.A. of New York has instituted a course of instruction on the automobile, for women.

A few months ago when the war cloud was not so heavy and hung not so low the course was not as complete as it is now. The present program takes in everything about the automobile, A to Z, driving, repairing, etc.

Within a few weeks the women taking the course will be graduate chauffeurs and mechanicians and will be ready then, to drive automobiles or ambulances or anything other sort of motor vehicle to which they may be assigned.

The Countess Ida Cohen D'Envers treating a wounded soldier at
Verona. She introduced the new Andrine treatment for shell
burns into Italy, a method which has been utilised by the French
Government with such wonderful success.
TRAINING THE NEW LAND ARMY

These young women whose patriotism has moved them to become farm hands, are seen at a training school near Theydon Bois Essex. They work here a month until they acquire a goodserviceable knowledge of the duties required of them and are then drafted elsewhere. Special attention is devoted to milving, as clumsy fingers could easily spoil a milch cow. Our Photo Shows, milking dummy cows to give the fingers the necessary delicacy of touch.
